patches.value: One representation throughout: a Coeff is the normalized complex Fourier coefficient sequence indexed by ℤ, with conjugate symmetry for reality and coefficient zero at zero for mean zero. H s is weighted square summability with weight (1+k²)^s, and hn is the square root of that sum; dh/dn are the homogeneous versions restricted away from zero. This is exactly the completion-of-polynomials model in D003, including negative orders. contH and convH state continuity/convergence in these weighted norms, not pointwise coefficient topology. smooth means membership in every nonnegative integer Sobolev space, equivalent to a smooth periodic function; smoothCurve and smoothPair express norm continuity and C¹ dependence at every such order. All displayed series and integrals are mathematical noncomputable definitions; consumers must establish the guarded summability, integrability and boundedness, which are included in the output obligations when substantive. No default tsum or sSup value is used as an analytic conclusion without the appropriate domain. mul is spatial multiplication in coefficients, air is S_t, and invD is zero on mode zero. The unfiltered scheme and finite iterates are explicit formulas, with no unspecified solver or algebraic capabilities. weakD is the coefficientwise integrated weak derivative with the absolutely continuous representative. aeH supplies coefficient measurability, a.e. Hilbert membership and an essential bound; separability of weighted ℓ² identifies this with the usual Bochner L∞ condition. essH uses ENNReal essential supremum then toReal only on these bounded domains; xn uses essential norms, while supH concerns actual continuous value representatives. piecewise allows separate derivative extensions at knots and identifies the global derivative only a.e. on each piece. solution uses the physical normalized equation's coefficient integral identity; for s≥0 C H^s this is equivalent to the distributional equation because the L² product has absolutely convergent convolution coefficients. exact adds uniform-in-time L² convergence from smooth solutions for the Fourier cutoffs of q, expressing the fixed smooth-approximation solution convention without granting existence. Uniqueness is EqOn on [0,T], so arbitrary values of a Curve outside its horizon never affect the result. sign=1 denotes target u_t+u_xxx=∂x(u²)/2, sign=-1 denotes the source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx; this is an actual equation-sign parameter, not a regularity assumption. No M ports or background-note premises are introduced. Native type probes verified these complete predicates with no missing parameters. The ℝ powers in the weights and estimates are Real.rpow; natural powers of complex Fourier multipliers are ordinary monoid powers. The membership predicate uses real Summable rather than overloading an lp parameter: the inspected Memℓp definition uses an ENNReal exponent (zero means finite support and infinity means boundedness), so neither is silently used as Sobolev order. All frequency indices and grid indices are explicitly ℤ and ℕ respectively; n≥0 is intrinsic to ℕ, and L>0 is a proposition, not a truncated integer division. Complex scalar action on coefficients is pointwise; real coefficients in scalar actions are explicitly cast to ℂ.
